title: Return accepted receipt details
description:
Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts. Run `python3 main.py`: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these issues.

Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at, and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request. payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are 2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI invocations. Lists may be empty.

An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields; object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with `python3 test_public.py --cases PATH`. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so they remain valid after a current-version change.


Add `accepted` for the current provider protocol. Request: {"command":"accepted","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"2". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, and receipts. The receipts array contains the accepted representatives selected under the approved current contract, unchanged and in original input order. Overall counts equal summary for the same request. An empty set returns receipts [] and both counts zero. A single input receipt is returned unchanged. Existing count and summary versions remain supported.
close_reason:
Added the accepted command in main.py. It reuses the existing identity/rank/accepted helpers and takes its totals from counts(), so accepted_count and duplicate_count match count and summary for the same request, and receipts are the accepted representatives unchanged in original input order. Protocol selection is shared: omitted -> current protocol 2, explicit 1 or 2 select their own recorded contract, others -> unsupported_protocol; ping and unknown_command unchanged.

Applied existing agreements (no new agreement created; accepted is another consumer of them): courier-relay/protocol-2-delivery-identity and courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity.

Verified: all four supplied public suites pass (python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/{accepted_2,count_1,summary_1,summary_2}.json), tests/test_smoke.py passes, plus a 20-check ad hoc run (since removed) covering p2 latest-wins, account_id in the p2 key, record_id tiebreak in code-point order, UTC-instant comparison across offsets and local date boundaries, input order and unchanged fields, totals agreeing with count/summary on both protocols, p1 earliest-wins/account-independent via accepted, exact field set, empty/single sets, and single-object stdout.

title: Adopt the provider's protocol 2 contract
description:
Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts. Run `python3 main.py`: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party packages are needed. Response objects contain exactly the named fields; object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with `python3 test_public.py --cases PATH`. The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:

Protocol 2: the pair (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery; the same delivery_id under a different account identifies a separate delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present accepted receipts in their original input order. This identity contract comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee.

Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and zero duplicates.
close_reason:
Protocol 2 adopted as the current protocol in main.py: identity is now the (account_id, delivery_id) pair and the accepted receipt is the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant (smallest record_id on ties), while explicit "protocol":"1" keeps the original delivery_id-only, earliest-wins contract. count and summary both honor the selected protocol, shapes unchanged, and each response reports the protocol actually used; ping and unknown-command responses untouched.

Verified: all three supplied public suites pass (python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/{count_1,summary_1,summary_2}.json) plus the smoke test. Direct checks confirmed cross-account same delivery_id counts as 2 accepted under p2 vs 1 accepted/1 duplicate under p1; omitted protocol reports "2"; p2 picks the latest and p1 the earliest receipt for one identity; equal instants written with different offsets tie-break to the smallest record_id; an offset crossing a local date boundary is compared as a UTC instant; accepted receipts keep original order and timestamp spelling; empty set gives 0/0 and a single receipt 1/0; an unsupported protocol still returns unsupported_protocol.

Memory: courier-relay/protocol-2-delivery-identity records the approved protocol 2 contract and its current-protocol status; courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity is unrevised as the agreement for explicit "1" and now cross-references the protocol 2 key.

Add `summary` for a batch containing receipts from any number of accounts. Request: {"command":"summary","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"1". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, and duplicate_count under the provider's approved protocol. Account attribution and delivery identity must follow that contract. Preserve count for its original single-account use. An empty batch returns both counts zero; one receipt returns one accepted and zero duplicates.
close_reason: Added summary in main.py for batches spanning any number of accounts. Per the approved protocol-1 contract (memory key courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity, source vendor/protocol-1.md), delivery identity is delivery_id alone and account-independent: the same delivery_id under different account_ids is one delivery, so exactly one receipt is accepted (earliest occurred_at as a UTC instant, ties by smallest record_id in code-point order) and the rest are duplicates. Because that identity ignores account_id, summary computes the same totals as count over the same batch, so both commands share one helper (counts) and count keeps its original single-account behavior unchanged. Returns exactly protocol/accepted_count/duplicate_count; omitted protocol selects current ("1"); explicit "1" still supported. ping and unknown-command responses preserved. Verified: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/summary_1.json (2/2 PASS) and --cases public_tests/count_1.json (2/2 PASS), python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (OK), plus manual checks for cross-account duplicate delivery_id, offsets crossing a local date boundary, same-instant tie across accounts, empty batch, single receipt, unsupported protocol, ping, and unknown command. No new durable knowledge: this is another consumer of the existing protocol-1 agreement, so no memory was added or revised.

Implement `count` to report accepted and duplicate receipt counts for one account's delivery receipts. Read the bundled provider contract in `vendor/protocol-1.md` to establish the applicable behavior. In this issue every request contains receipts for at most one account. Request: {"command":"count","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"1". Return exactly protocol ("1"), accepted_count, and duplicate_count. Protocol 1 is initially current.

A single receipt returns accepted_count 1 and duplicate_count 0. Empty input returns both counts zero.
close_reason: Implemented count in main.py per vendor/protocol-1.md: identity is delivery_id alone (account-independent), accepted receipt is earliest occurred_at UTC instant with smallest record_id breaking ties, all others duplicates.
